study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose and evaluate a whole-brain normative modeling approach (FUNCOIN) for resting-state fMRI functional connectivity to detect individual-level abnormalities in complex brain disorders, and assess its clinical relevance in bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of abnormality rates (outlier proportions) between BD/PD and healthy controls; analysis of abnormality vs years before PD diagnosis using scan-to-diagnosis intervals.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: BD and PD subjects show significantly higher likelihood of abnormal whole-brain FC patterns than controls; PD abnormalities are detectable up to 8 years before diagnosis; localized edgewise models did not show these effects.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using a FUNCOIN-based normative model trained on UKB healthy subjects, the authors found BD and PD groups were significantly more likely to exhibit abnormal FC deviations than healthy subjects. BD subjects stratified into two distinct subgroups characterized by opposing deviation directions across the first two components. In PD, abnormal FC patterns were significant even on scans up to 8 years prior to diagnosis, indicating potential pre-diagnostic signatures. Comparable localized (edgewise) normative approaches failed to detect these group-level effects.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Interpretation of Z-scores is challenging (directionality unknown a priori); difficult to determine clinical relevance of individual outliers; some diseased subjects may not be outliers; only linear covariate effects modeled; nonlinear effects not explored.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: As in other normative modelling studies of FC, interpretation of the Z-scores can be challenging ... we only consider linear effects on FC ... There may be diagnostic information in nonlinear effects ...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Whole-brain, component-level normative modeling (FUNCOIN) avoids massive multiple testing by jointly performing dimensionality reduction and regression on FC; implementation available as a Python package; covariates include sex, age, and their interaction; site effects can be included if needed.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Training/testing split: 32,000/14,000 healthy UKB subjects; four scanning sites (harmonized acquisition). UKB ICA parcellation with 55 components; 490 time points per scan (6 minutes), with initial 8 time points removed; 502 subjects had 532 time points before truncation. Site-effect sensitivity analysis (supplementary) indicated negligible impact on primary components (g1, g2). Clinical groups: BD (ICD-10 F31, N=101) and PD (ICD-10 G20, N=132) from UKB.
